history.dynasty: Early Chera Kingdom (Chera Chenguttuvan, c. 180 CE, per tradition)
history.period: Traditionally c. 1st-2nd century CE (~2000 years old; archaeological verification lacking)
history.summary: Ancient hilltop shrine deep inside the Periyar Tiger Reserve on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border, at ~1337 m elevation, dedicated to Kannagi, the heroine of the Tamil epic Cilappatikaram. Legend says Kannagi came to this spot (Vannathipara) after burning Madurai to avenge her husband Kovalan and ascended to heaven from here in a Pushpaka Vimana; Chera king Chenguttuvan consecrated the temple as 'Kannagi Kottam' around 2,000 years ago, and his narration to Ilango Adigal is said to have inspired the Silappatikaram. The temple shows Pandyan architecture with massive stone boundary walls and steps. It is open for worship ONLY on Chitra Pournami day each year (joint Kerala/Tamil Nadu pujaris; priests from both states perform the puja). name: Mangala Devi Temple
town_description: Kumily is a town in Idukki district, Kerala, adjoining Thekkady at the edge of the Periyar Tiger Reserve. It is the main gateway for spice plantations, Periyar lake boating and the Mangala Devi temple trek, about 12-14 km by jeep into the forest.
